This file documents the structures resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =structures=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 42329792-D417-5831-81F1-864B3233A803
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
structures list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =trading.v1.structures.list=.

#+name: structures-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle structures-list.ores :exports none
structures list --limit 1
#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 8A174011-2452-51DE-A11F-A46657D8A495
:END:

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
structures get <id>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =trading.v1.structures.get=.

#+name: structures-get
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle structures-get.ores :exports none
structures get 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
#+end_src

** =get-many=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 1329754B-CF25-57B8-BDD8-16F3057D4ADD
:END:

Reads several rows in one request, one key group per row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
structures get-many <id>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =trading.v1.structures.get_many=.

#+name: structures-get-many
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle structures-get-many.ores :exports none
structures get-many 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
#+end_src
